title: The next-action slice leaves the legacy AC allocation, the daily check Schedule, the DL22 durations and the role-class field unspecified
source: Legacy RWB-E2-035 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 035 Next action on the case v2.md); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P3 Case and workflow v4.md A2.50 and A2.51 (AC-P3-050, AC-P3-051); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3.md API-P3-016 and DF-CAS-049 to DF-CAS-053; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 14 (P3 contract row) and slide 41 (P3 ownership row); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slide 14 (durable timer) and slide 44 (JOB-05 retired); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (legacy RWB-E2-035, slice RWB-P3-E2035-APP, acs []); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-03, DP-04 and DP-10 and R7.3
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.6 Schedules; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability
description: Five values of this slice are not in the sources. (1) The plan allocates no legacy acceptance criterion of RWB-E2-035 to any slice: every slice of the key carries acs [], so AC1 to AC14 have no owning new story and this slice writes new criteria. (2) The time of day of the DailyCaseRun Schedule that replaces the retired five-minute JOB-05 check is not stated. (3) The DL22 service-level duration per route state is not in the sources; the legacy story seeds 5 working days per state and marks it assumed. (4) The field of the rwb-access answer that carries a role class is not stated, and BR5 needs the class to decide waiting. (5) The legacy story reads a role table directly and the target reads it through the rwb-access contract, so the call and its cache have no stated field list.
evidence: split_plan.json: RWB-E2-035 slices RWB-P2-E2035-CON, RWB-P2-E2035-APP, RWB-P4-E2035-APP, RWB-P3-E2035-APP, RWB-P7-E2035-APP, RWB-P2-E2035-OPS and RWB-ITG-E2035-ITG all carry acs []. FSD P3 v4 A2.50 and A2.51 carry the same feature and criteria but no schedule. TSD P3 v3 API-P3-016 gives the operation and DF-CAS-049 to DF-CAS-053 give the five next-action fields, and neither gives a duration. Legacy story section 3: 'Until the business values are loaded it is seeded with 5 working days for each state of the route sets in force (assumed)'. Legacy section 12: 'RoleInfo ReferenceData.role(String roleCode)' with no field list of an access answer.
proposed: Keep all five as data or defaults: DL22 values loaded by RW-REFADM, the check as a DailyCaseRun step at a time of day agreed with OPS, the role class from the rwb-access answer, and the legacy criteria proved by RWB-ITG-E2035-ITG.

title: The placement slice leaves the legacy AC allocation, the approved callers list, the production matrix grant, the overflow shape, the caller mapping and the login name unspecified
source: Legacy RWB-E2-036 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 036 Queue write interface for models and agents v1.md); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P3 Case and workflow v4.md A2.52 (AC-P3-052); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3.md API-P3-012 (POST /queues/{queueId}/placements); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 14 and slide 41 (P3 ownership row); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api POST /queues/{queueId}/placements, owner P3; queue, assignment and recovery_case owner P3); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (slice RWB-P3-E2036-APP, acs []); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-08 and DP-09
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan
description: Six values of this slice are not in the sources. (1) The plan allocates no legacy acceptance criterion of RWB-E2-036 to any slice (acs [] everywhere), so the fourteen criteria of this story are new. (2) The approved callers list is empty at go-live and only its legacy configuration key rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers is known. (3) The production permission matrix gives SY-AGENT Queue and allocation R only, so a matrix version change is needed before the first caller. (4) The 201 answer of the overflow path has no field list beyond the legacy note that it carries the overflow queue ID and no assignment. (5) How a caller code and its type resolve to a service identity is not specified. (6) The name, grants and secret reference of the rwb-case login are not specified.
evidence: split_plan.json: all seven slices of RWB-E2-036 carry acs []. Legacy story section 3: 'The list is empty at go-live (assumed)' and 'The matrix today gives SY-AGENT R only'. Legacy section 12: 'Response 201 ... the response is then the placement result with the overflow queue ID and no assignment (response change recorded in the additions file)' with no field list. TSD P3 v3 API-P3-012 gives the request fields and the rights but no identity mapping and no login name.
proposed: Hold the six as configuration, contract or deployment values: the callers list as a parameter, the matrix version by RW-SECADM, the overflow shape in the contract story, the caller mapping in RWB-P2-E2036-CON, the login name in the platform DB story, and the legacy criteria in RWB-ITG-E2036-ITG.

title: The encumbrance-check slice leaves the requirement ID, the check-versus-state boundary, the S2 answer shape, the rule timer specs and three new field IDs unspecified
source: Legacy RWB-E3-013 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md lines 2163 to 2261); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2.md lines 171 and 181 (R-SET-22 and R-DIL-01 transition rows); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3.md FEAT-TRT-13; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 14 and slide 41; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 recovery_case DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (slice RWB-P3-E3013-APP, acs [], C RWB-S2-E3013-CON); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-03 and DP-05
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 18 Traceability
description: Six values of this slice are not in the sources. (1) The Epics 3 to 8 story RWB-E3-013 carries no requirement ID, so nothing is traceable to a REQ. (2) No source says which service owns the encumbrance and title check and which the case state move. (3) The S2 operation that returns the check answer has no path, verb or field list. (4) The TSD S2 v2 transition table gives from-state, event code and to-state for R-SET-22 and R-DIL-01 but no timer spec, so the task due date has no stated source. (5) The three case-side columns the slice needs (check_ref, check_outcome_code, decision_record_id) have no LDM field IDs. (6) The name of the local timeout parameter of the call is not stated.
evidence: Epics 3 to 8 v3 RWB-E3-013 metadata block: Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on, Decision - no requirement row. TSD S2 v2: 'R-SET-22 | COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED | TITLE_DOCUMENTS_MISSING | COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED' and 'R-DIL-01 | ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL | ROUTE_APPROVED | EARLY_READINESS_CHECK' with no timer column. API Specification v4 lists GET /treatments/{treatmentId} for S2 but no check operation. LDM v8 recovery_case range DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 holds no check field.
proposed: Read the boundary as S2 owns the check and P3 owns the state, the task and the decision record; let RWB-S2-E3013-CON fix the operation and its fields; take the timer spec from the answer; add the three columns in the P3 migration and ask the data owner for field IDs; use the platform one-hop 2 s default until a parameter is named.

title: The split of the proof-of-delivery key between rwb-case, rwb-litigation and rwb-comms, the S4 answer, the notice-period duration and the requirement ID are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E5-002 in 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (data table, endpoints and screens but no requirement ID); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.2 (R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09, served_result) and A2.2.3.3; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md (transition table; line 'Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices'); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 41 (P6 owns notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery), slide 17 (rwb_comms schema) and slide 19 (rwb_litigation IN and OUT); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (notice, merge_field and template P6; recovery_case, timer and task P3); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.md (DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023, DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036)
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability
description: The legacy story RWB-E5-002 was written inside one monolith: it wrote the delivery confirmation onto the case, started the notice period from delivered_at and wrote the decision log entry, and its data table mixed the case, the timer, the notice, the customer view and the decision log. In the target the fact is cut three ways and no source states the cut. (1) The write side is split: Architecture v5 slide 41 and the ownership map give the notice, the template, the merge fields and the proof of delivery to rwb-comms (P6), while the case state, the timer and the task belong to rwb-case (P3) and the legal action to rwb-litigation (S4); no source says which service records the delivery answer nor what rwb-case keeps of it. (2) The hand-over is not specified: the WP records RWB-S4-E5002-CON as the contract dependency of this story and the story consumes the proof-of-delivery answer, but the TSD S4 says calls go through the published Java interfaces with P3 for the case, which points the other way, and no source names the operation, the verb or the fields of the answer. (3) The notice-period duration is not in any source: the legacy story starts 'the notice period' and the S4 TSD names the states and event codes but gives no duration and no reference row; the story takes it from a SERVICE_LEVEL reference row of rwb-case, whose code and value are unknown. (4) The legacy story master of Epics 3 to 8 carries no requirement ID for RWB-E5-002 (feature, module, data, endpoints, screens, rights and test cases only), so traceability cannot run to a REQ identifier even though the FSD S4 module states REQ-S4-001 for the notice family. (5) The module extracts named in the WP exist (FSD P3 Case and workflow v4, TSD P3 Case and workflow v3) but neither carries the proof-of-delivery material: it sits in the S4 module extracts (FSD S4 A2.2) and in the P6 communications extract, so the P3 module files do not answer any of the questions above.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E5-002 has no REQ row and no requirement column; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 41 row P6 'notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery' and slide 17 'writes schema rwb_comms: notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery'; TSD S4 v2 line 156 'Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices'; FSD S4 v3 A2.2.3.1 rows R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09 with no duration and no service split; grep of the P3 FSD v4 and P3 TSD v3 shows no proof-of-delivery section, while the S4 FSD A2.2 and A2.3 carry it; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json notice and merge_field owner P6, recovery_case and timer owner P3.
proposed: Confirm with the S4 and P6 contract owners that rwb-litigation answers the delivery outcome on its own base /api/recovery/litigation/v1 and that rwb-case stores only the notice reference, the delivery date and the outcome on recovery_case, with the notice row, the proof and the barcode staying in rwb_comms; publish the operation path and fields in RWB-S4-E5002-CON; put the notice-period duration in a SERVICE_LEVEL reference row of rwb-case with RW-COE as owner; attach the REQ identifier to this feature in the EP05 PRD (C1).

title: The committee routing of RWB-E6-017 crosses two services with no operation, no committee queue code, no meeting timer type and no requirement ID in the sources
source: Legacy RWB-E6-017 (Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3, lines 9829 to 9924); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P3 contract row), slide 20 (S7 contract row) and slide 41 (the P3 and S7 ownership rows); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 14 (CaseWorkflow, EvaluateRules, RecordAndApply, durable timer) and slide 23 (S7 write-off, committee, JOB-16 Schedule); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (write_off S7, deviation S8, queue and recovery_case and task and timer P3); _work/msr/extract FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 and TSD P3 Case and workflow v3; Template and Rules v1 ?R5.5 DP-01, DP-03, DP-13 and DP-19
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.6 Schedules; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability
description: The legacy story keeps the scan, the pack, the route, the committee queue, the meeting booking, the case state and the decision log in one module: it sends the pack to the committee queue and books it into the monthly meeting, and the case moves to WITH_COMMITTEE by R-WO-11 or to CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM by R-WO-06 in the same process. In the target the write-off route set, the committee and the pack are S7's (rwb-writeoff) while the case, the queue, the task and the timer are P3's (rwb-case), so the routing answer has to cross a service boundary and no source says how. Six values are missing. (1) The FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 and TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 extracts named in the WP exist under _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6 and _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, and hold no committee routing value: they cover the case record, the CMMN state, queues, allocation, timers and the case view, and name the write-off collection queues only in passing, so the module content the WP assumes for this story is not in them. (2) The legacy story carries no requirement ID, so nothing ties the case side to a requirement. (3) Which service owns the committee and the meeting booking (S7) against the case state and the queue (P3) is stated only by the Architecture v5 slide 41 rows, and no operation between the two services exists in the sources. (4) Whether the booking date is a Temporal Schedule or a durable timer is not stated: the Schedules of Architecture v5 slide 44 name only JOB-16, and the durable-timer pattern of the Temporal design is described for the stage clocks. (5) The committee queue code is in no list: the queue template and the FSD P3 examples name the write-off collection queue (WO-BKK-CO) and the deviation handler queue (DEV-HANDLER) but no committee queue, and LOV-TIMER holds no committee-meeting timer type. (6) The S7 operation path, its method and the names of its request and answer fields are not written in any source read, because the S7 contract story has not fixed them.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14: the P3 row lists REST GET /cases/{id}, /cases?queue=, POST /cases/{id}/actions, GET /tasks, POST /tasks/{id}/complete and GET /case-summary/{id}, and no write-off or committee cell; slide 20: the S7 row lists GET/POST /write-offs and POST /write-offs/{id}/submit and no case operation. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41: P3 owns case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation, timers; S7 owns eligibility, committee, posting, recovery after charge-off; the connection matrix has no P3 to S7 cell and no S7 to P3 cell. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 line for JOB-16: monthly, third working day, rwb-writeoff, Schedule. Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 23: the S7 route step is 'Committee decides R-WO-11 to 17', and the note says JOB-16 is a Temporal Schedule in rwb-writeoff. LOV-TIMER (Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8, lines 1629 to 1637) lists SERVICE_LEVEL, NOTICE_PERIOD, CURE_PERIOD, PRESCRIPTION, HEARING_DEADLINE, OFFER_VALIDITY, HOLDING_AGE, CLAIM_DEADLINE and INSTALLMENT_DUE, and no committee-meeting type. FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 lines 621, 1547 and 712 name the queue template with 12 queues for the TDR, DIL, litigation, NPA, debt sale and write-off teams, queue WO-BKK-CO and queue DEV-HANDLER, and no committee queue. Legacy RWB-E6-017: the story block holds no requirement ID, and its two endpoints are the write-off committee-decision and write-off-scans operations of the monolith.
proposed: rwb-case serves and applies the case side of the routing answer as one operation of RWB-S7-E6017-CON, and the S7 contract story fixes the path, the method and the field names; the S7 contract fake answers with them until the contract lands. The committee queue row and the committee-meeting timer type are added to the rwb-case reference data by RW-COE and read as rows, not as code. The meeting date is a durable timer of CaseWorkflow and no Schedule is registered; JOB-16 stays the only write-off Schedule and it stays in rwb-writeoff. The committee, the pack, the amount, the tax criteria and the approval stay with S7, and rwb-case stores only the meeting reference, its date and the queue. The requirement trace goes through FEAT-WOF-05 and the rules R-WO-11 and R-WO-06 until a requirement ID is allocated.
